docs.title: Framework overview
docs.text:
Capability Go implementation Registration Generic typed function registration or explicit FunctionDefinition Middleware Ordered handlers with options and context Set/Get; startup-only registration Schemas Native schema builders/struct metadata, HTTP input/output checks HTTP fasthttp server and net/http adapter, optional custom routes Uploads Multipart routing, bounds, temporary-file ownership and typed file injection IPC Unix newline/length framing, bounded stdio and maintained Node client Documentation Global enable/path controls, function and middleware schema views Tooling Go CLI initialization/generators, tests, standalone SDK resolution

Node/Bun engine, HTTP client/React SDK and Go/Node IPC example are distinct integration paths. A browser uses HTTP, while a local Node daemon client can use Unix IPC. HTTP File/Blob uploads do not become live file objects over JSON IPC.

Typed native functions and schema contracts behind one RPC endpoint, with middleware, multipart handling, Unix IPC and server-rendered documentation.

Version v1.0.2 adds bounded 2 MiB stdio framing to the hardening fixes; see installation. Go >=1.27.4 is required. Node 24 LTS is the primary sibling/client test runtime; Bun is tested independently in the Node framework.

  • Functions, schemas, middleware
  • IPC, in-memory testing, custom routes
  • Docs controls, API, deployment
  • Protocol, benchmark context

IsPublic is deprecated and ignored. All authentication/authorization is enforced by application middleware, not documentation metadata or caller-injected context.

docs.title: For contributors
docs.text: Start with contribution policy, development setup and the internal source map. The sidebar separates end-user usage from implementation, testing and release guides. See the security policy and Code of Conduct before opening a report.

docs.title: Start an application
docs.text:
go install github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go/cmd/crpc-go@v1.0.2
crpc-go init my-api
cd my-api
go mod tidy
go build ./...
go test ./...
crpc-go dev

The versioned CLI selects SDKv1.0.2. Register typed functions and middleware before serving; use native schemas for input/output contracts. For direct server setup, see the repository README. Review middleware, schemas, HTTP routes and IPC for application integration.

Go uses native metadata rather than TypeBox. Middleware header/options schemas describe documentation; middleware remains responsible for validating them. fasthttp buffers transport intake; per-request bounds are not an aggregate-memory guarantee. See lifecycle and source architecture for implementation details.

docs.title: Public API reference
docs.text: Module version: github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go@v1.0.2; see installation. Go >=1.27.4 is required.

docs.title: rpc
docs.text:
New(Config) requires an explicit RpcPath and non-nil CORS policy. Configure Host/Port, DocsEnabled/DocsPath, request/file limits, timeouts, proxy trust and optional UseHttpStatusCodes. Core Config reads no environment variables.

API Purpose Register(FunctionConfig[I,O]) Typed function wrapper/global registration app.RegisterFunction / RegisterMiddleware Explicit instance registration app.UseGlobalRegistry Import init-registered modules app.Handler / NetHTTPHandler fasthttp / net-http handlers app.ListenAndServe / Shutdown Native server lifecycle app.GET/POST/PUT/DELETE Custom func(*HTTPContext) error handlers app.CallInMemory Populate output target through the execution pipeline NewTestCaller, Call, CallRaw In-memory test helpers

MiddlewareFn is func(*Context,map[string]string,map[string]any) error. Store trusted state with Context.Set/Get or GetContext[T]. Caller data/legacy bypass fields never establish identity. Middleware metadata schemas describe contracts; Go does not apply new automatic option/header validation.

NewError(code,message,details...) creates application errors. Default HTTP status for handled RPC failures is200; opt-in mapping, transport errors and custom-route statuses differ. Inspect envelope status/code, not HTTP status alone.

UploadedFile has methods OriginalFilename, Filename, Size, TempPath, MimeType, DeclaredMimeType, DetectedMimeType, Bytes, Reader, SaveTo and Cleanup. Size and Filename are methods, not fields. SaveTo creates a new 0600 destination without overwriting; choose a unique application-owned path. Framework cleanup removes the temporary input, not the copy you persist with SaveTo.

docs.title: schema and nodebridge
docs.text:
SchemaRule exposes native structural/constraint metadata. Use String/Number/ Integer/Boolean/Object/Array/File/Optional, FromStruct and their fluent methods; examples are in schemas. IsPublic remains an ignored deprecated bool on FunctionMetadata; no visibility/auth replacement is introduced.

nodebridge.ServeUnixSocket(app,path) serves bounded Unix frames. GenerateTypeScriptDeclarations takes app.Functions() and returns a declaration string; there is no export:types CLI command. See IPC for the maintained Node client and framing.

docs.title: Architecture and protocol
docs.text:
The configured HTTP endpoint accepts {namespace,functionName,data}. Functions register explicitly, then dispatch through middleware, input validation, the handler and output validation. Authentication/authorization are application middleware responsibilities, also enforced for in-memory/IPC execution.

Success uses {status:"ok",data,meta?}. Handled RPC application errors default to HTTP 200 with {status:"error",code,message,details?}. UseHttpStatusCodes is an explicit opt-in; transport/framing failures, custom routes and docs404 differ. This is not a proxy caching/security guarantee.

JSON objects, arrays, scalars and explicit null preserve shape. Omitted HTTP data defaults to {}; null reaches schema validation/handlers as nil. Other transports' omission/output conventions remain existing behavior. Native schemas are not a complete TypeBox/JSON Schema implementation; compare the actual shared contracts.

HTTP uses encoding/json/v2 for its envelope/serialization. Other in-memory/IPC paths use existing encoding/json conventions. Do not claim duplicate-member, nil slice/map, number or allocation behavior is identical across every transport. Output validation remains active; application custom marshalers need real tests.

fasthttp buffers transport intake before application multipart streaming. The net/http adapter is not a guarantee of end-to-end streaming. Header/body routing must agree and duplicates fail before dispatch; headerless routing is supported. Only top-level/direct-array file transport is supported. Per-request bounds and cleanup are not a concurrent aggregate-memory guarantee or content sanitization.

Unix IPC frames are bounded 2MiB, with deadlines and cleanup. The Node example client rejects connection-level failures without replay. A credential/identity cannot bypass middleware by arriving as a caller-supplied context object.

Docs are controlled globally. IsPublic is retained/deprecated/ignored, not a visibility/auth flag. Safe structural middleware docs omit configured values and defaults without executing handlers or changing runtime schema behavior.

docs.title: Benchmark context
docs.text:
Historical workloads/results live under the repository's benchmarks directory. Retain commit, Go/runtime version, hardware, CPU/memory limits, payload shape, concurrency and warmup when reproducing them. They are not a current latency, throughput, zero-allocation or security guarantee. No new production benchmark was run as part of release stabilization.

Account for transport-buffered fasthttp intake and runtime-buffered Node Fetch formData when comparing memory. HTTP JSON v2 versus IPC JSON v1 conventions also need workload-specific tests; see architecture.

docs.title: Our Pledge
docs.text:
We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

docs.title: Our Standards
docs.text:

  • Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
  • Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
  • Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
  • Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
  • Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community

  • Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
  • Public or private harassment
  • Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission

docs.title: Enforcement Responsibilities
docs.text:
Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces. Examples of representing our community include using an official e-mail address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the community leaders responsible for enforcement at info@cellsweb.com or the CellsWeb contact page. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

docs.title: Enforcement Guidelines
docs.text: Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:

docs.title: 1. Correction
docs.text:
Community Impact: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.

Consequence: A private, written warning from community leaders, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.

docs.title: 2. Warning
docs.text:
Community Impact: A violation through a single incident or series of actions.

Consequence: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.

docs.title: 3. Temporary Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: A serious violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior.

Consequence: A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public communication with the community for a specified period of time. No public or private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.

docs.title: 4. Permanent Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals.

Consequence: A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within the community.

docs.title: Contributing to CellsWeb RPC Go
docs.text: Welcome. Small corrections, reproducible bug reports, tests and focused features are useful contributions. Read the Code of Conduct and security policy. Security-sensitive reports must be private. See the MIT LICENSE before including third-party material.

docs.title: Go development setup
docs.text:
Use Go 1.27.4 or newer compatible tooling; Go 1.27.4 was validated. Node 24.15.0 and npm are needed for example-node; that example's lockfile resolves TypeScript 5.9.3. Unix IPC suites require a Unix-domain-socket environment (validated macOSarm64). Node SDK work uses its own pnpm/TypeScript versions, not this example's lockfile.

git clone https://github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go.git
cd crpc-go
go mod download
go build ./...
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
go test -race -count=1 ./...
cd example-node
npm ci
npm run typecheck
CRPC_IPC_TEST_RACE=1 npm test

Use a fork and a focused branch. Preserve unrelated local work, and use a separate worktree for a pinned baseline. Race detection needs a working supported cgo/C compiler toolchain; record unsupported platforms instead of claiming a pass.

docs.title: Go repository map and conventions
docs.text:
• pkg/rpc: CoreRPC, configuration, registration, Context, HTTP/multipart, in-memory callers, typed wrappers, errors and docs renderer.
  • pkg/schema: native SchemaRule constructors, validation, multipart coercion and documentation export; this is not a complete TypeBox/JSON Schema interpreter.
  • pkg/nodebridge: Unix/stdio bridge and TypeScript declaration generator.
  • cmd/crpc-go: CLI dispatcher and init/dev/scaffold commands.
  • pkg/utils: storage and image helpers. example, example-mongo and benchmarks have separate Go modules; root go test ./... does not include nested modules.
  • example-node: maintained IPC client, typed contracts and actual-daemon tests.

Use gofmt, explicit errors and existing native schema abstractions. Preserve Context ownership and cleanup. Register functions/middleware before serving; do not assume live registry mutation is a supported concurrency model. Prefer focused changes over pipeline/renderer refactoring in an unrelated fix.

docs.title: Create a Go function or middleware
docs.text:
Build the local CLI, generate a disposable app and select the local SDK deliberately:

go build -o /tmp/crpc-go-dev ./cmd/crpc-go
/tmp/crpc-go-dev init /tmp/crpc-contributor-app
cd /tmp/crpc-contributor-app
go work init . /absolute/path/to/crpc-go
/tmp/crpc-go-dev create:function --ns catalog --name get
/tmp/crpc-go-dev create:middleware --name tenantResolver --desc 'Resolve tenant'
go build ./...

Replace the absolute checkout path. Do not commit machine-specific workspaces. Source/VCS-built CLIs intentionally select older SDK v1.0.0 without a workspace; the versioned v1.0.2 CLI selects SDK v1.0.2. Check go list -m, not just the CLI display. Generated Go functions require explicit imports/registration; there is no Node-style filesystem discovery or --middlewares CLI flag.

docs.title: Test and regression workflow
docs.text:
First reproduce a bug at a recorded baseline, then add a failing regression. Use table-driven shapes/invalid inputs and assert middleware/handler call order, error code/details, HTTP status, resource bounds and cleanup. Important gates:

go test -count=1 ./pkg/rpc -run TestHTTPJSONPayloadShapes
go test -count=1 ./pkg/rpc -run TestCallRaw
go test -count=1 ./pkg/nodebridge
CRPC_STANDALONE_INTEGRATION=1 go test -count=1 ./...
CRPC_STANDALONE_INTEGRATION=1 CRPC_SCAFFOLD_RACE=1 go test -race -count=1 ./...

The standalone flag resolves the actual public source-build fallback SDK and then an explicit local workspace; it needs network access and an unused port 4000. The race flag instruments generated child servers too. example-node has separate npm build/typecheck/tests; CRPC_IPC_TEST_RACE=1 instruments its real daemon. Nested examples need their own build/test commands and, for local SDK changes, an explicit workspace. Do not claim database integration passed from a build.

docs.title: Changes involving both runtimes
docs.text:
Use semantic parity, not identical implementation. Read the sibling Node contributor guide. Propose protocol/default/public-API changes before implementation; identify the migration/version implications. Attach equivalent logical fixtures and actual results for Node and Go. Go's checked-in pkg/rpc/testdata/http-json-shapes.json is a useful fixture set, with HTTP tests in that package and Node union regressions in rpc-core. There is no checked-in one-command cross-repository parity runner; do not require a private review-kit path from external contributors.

Preserve these compatibility boundaries unless explicitly reviewed/versioned:

  • One configurable RPC endpoint with {namespace,functionName,data}. Arbitrary JSON data shapes survive; omitted HTTP data defaults to {}, explicit null stays null for schema validation. Do not silently coerce ordinary JSON inputs.
  • Successfully handled application errors use HTTP200 by default. Opt-in status mapping and transport/framework errors are distinct; not every malformed body automatically produces HTTP400. Preserve success/error envelopes and SDK parsing.
  • Middleware owns authentication/authorization. Remote callers cannot skip it or inject trusted state. Missing configured middleware fails closed.
  • Multipart routing headers come as a pair and agree with required body routing. Headerless fallback puts routing fields before files. No application-owned upload files before required authorization, and no cleanup/size-limit weakening.
  • Client files are top-level fields/direct arrays; nested file objects require a deliberate versioned design. Native Node streams, Fetch form parsing and Go transport buffering have different memory boundaries; do not promise zero RAM.
  • Node discovery and Go registration are intentionally different. isPublic/IsPublic remain deprecated/ignored compatibility fields; no replacement visibility flag.
  • IPC request IDs/framing remain compatible; never replay a failed call implicitly. Unix framing limits do not apply automatically to stdio.

docs.title: Pull requests and review
docs.text:
Open an issue/discussion first for a substantial architectural/API change. Keep one root cause per fix and include problem, before/after behavior, affected paths, compatibility and limitations. Conventional-style subjects such as fix:, docs: and test: help scanning; match existing style without rewriting unrelated files.

Use the PR template. Provide exact executed commands/outcomes, red/green evidence for bugs and both-runtime results where applicable. Docs-only PRs should run both strict MkDocs builds when shared content changes, validate links, render diagrams and compile meaningful examples; unnecessary implementation-mirroring tests are not required. Include screenshots for documentation UI changes. State untested scenarios/skips honestly. Never commit secrets, generated upload files, dist, node_modules, local workspaces or unrelated agent changes.

A maintainer reviews scope, protocol/API impact, tests, resource cleanup and docs before merge. Do not merge/publish/tag as part of an ordinary contribution. Release changes require separate approval and public-install verification. New public API fields/options and defaults require explicit compatibility review.

The contributor documentation contains source maps, request lifecycle, subsystem test maps and release guidance.

docs.title: Custom HTTP routes
docs.text:
Register custom handlers with func(*rpc.HTTPContext) error, not raw fasthttp callbacks. Custom routes have their own statuses/auth responsibilities; the uniform RPC application-error convention does not force them to return200.

package main

import (
    "log"
    _ "docsexamples/functions/hello"
    "github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go/pkg/rpc"
)
func main() {
    app, err := rpc.New(rpc.Config{RpcPath:"/rpc", Host:"127.0.0.1", Port:4000,
        DocsEnabled:false, CORS:&rpc.CorsConfig{AllowOrigins:[]string{"http://localhost:3000"}}})
    if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
    app.UseGlobalRegistry()
    app.GET("/health", func(c *rpc.HTTPContext) error { return c.SendString("OK") })
    app.POST("/example", func(c *rpc.HTTPContext) error { return c.Status(202).JSON(map[string]any{"accepted":true}) })
    if err := app.ListenAndServe(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
}

HTTPContext supplies Method, Path, Header, Query, Body, SetHeader, Status, JSON, SendString and Raw. Its Call method invokes registered RPCs in-process; validate custom-route credentials/signatures first and forward relevant credentials. A custom webhook handler does not become authenticated simply because it calls RPC.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Deploy the versioned v1.0.2 SDK with dependencies pinned in go.mod/go.sum. Use the matching versioned CLI for scaffolding. See installation and retain the deployment checks below.

go build -o dist/server ./cmd/server
NODE_ENV=production DOCS_ENABLED=false ./dist/server

Those env controls apply to the generated main. Programmatic rpc.Config reads no env automatically. Neither the binary nor crpc-go dev loads.env. Export trusted values explicitly. The generated listener is currently 0.0.0.0:4000 with /rpc; PORT/HOST/RPC_PATH in the env example are not consumed. Configure rpc.Config for another address/path, and match container/service/load-balancer ports to it.

Set an explicit CORS policy and application authentication/authorization. Configure request/file/time limits and proxy trust for the deployment. Disable docs globally when needed; metadata flags do not enforce security. Health/custom routes need their own exposure/auth policy. Inspect RPC envelope status in monitoring when using the default HTTP 200 convention; opt-in status mapping is separate.

Go >=1.27.4 is required. A Linux static build can use CGO_ENABLED=0 with the chosen GOOS/GOARCH; cross-compilation is not a runtime/container test. No untested Docker, cloud autoscaling, latency, resource-bound or deployment guarantee is made here. Use production workload/aggregate-memory measurements before choosing concurrency.

docs.text:
Read CONTRIBUTING for review requirements. This repository is a Go module; its example applications and Node IPC client have separate toolchains.

go mod download
go build ./...
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
go test -race -count=1 ./...
cd example-node
npm ci
npm run typecheck
CRPC_IPC_TEST_RACE=1 npm test

Full Unix IPC tests need a Unix socket environment. Race detection needs a working supported cgo/C toolchain. The release matrix was tested on macOSarm64; do not turn cross-compilation or a skipped suite into a runtime claim.

docs.title: Source CLI versus installed CLI
docs.text:
The versioned v1.0.2 CLI generates SDK v1.0.2. A local/VCS-built binary still uses its real older v1.0.0 SDK fallback, independent of display version. For local SDK development, generate an app with the source binary, then explicitly select this checkout with go work init . /absolute/path/to/crpc-go. Never commit that machine-specific workspace or edit go.mod to pretend an unpublished tag exists.

Register imported function/middleware packages and call UseGlobalRegistry before serving. Package init() only runs for imported packages. Changing a directory on disk does not cause Go discovery or restart an existing binary.

docs.title: Modules and optional integration
docs.text:
Root go test ./... does not traverse nested go.mod modules. example, example-mongo and benchmarks need their own commands; a successful build is not proof of a live database or benchmark result. Keep external-service tests scoped.

The explicitly enabled scaffold integration uses a real public dependency and then a local workspace, network access and port 4000. CRPC_SCAFFOLD_RACE=1 also instruments generated child servers. example-node's CRPC_IPC_TEST_RACE=1 similarly instruments its actual daemon. See the testing map.

docs.title: Build the documentation
docs.text:
python3 -m venv /tmp/crpc-docs-venv
/tmp/crpc-docs-venv/bin/python -m pip install mkdocs-material
/tmp/crpc-docs-venv/bin/mkdocs serve
/tmp/crpc-docs-venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict --site-dir /tmp/crpc-go-site

The existing deployment workflow installs Material; it is preserved. The versions above describe this validation, not a new Python dependency lock or CI job. Render Mermaid diagrams in a browser, validate links and compile executable examples as well as building strictly. Root policy snippets resolve from the repository root. See Node development for its different pnpm/TypeScript workspace setup.

docs.title: Functions and contracts
docs.text:
Go uses explicit registration. Contracts, middleware attachments and handlers can live in a co-located package; import it before UseGlobalRegistry. Examples below are compiled together as a small application.

package hello

import (
    "github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go/pkg/rpc"
    "github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go/pkg/schema"
)
type Input struct { Name string `json:"name" doc:"Caller name"` }
type Output struct { Greeting string `json:"greeting"` }
func init() {
    rpc.Register(rpc.FunctionConfig[Input, Output]{
        Namespace: "public", FunctionName: "hello",
        Metadata: rpc.FunctionMetadata{Description: "Greet a named caller"},
        InputSchema: schema.Object(map[string]*schema.SchemaRule{"name": schema.String().Min(1)}),
        OutputSchema: schema.FromStruct(Output{}), Handler: Run,
    })
}

package hello

import "github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go/pkg/rpc"
func Run(_ *rpc.Context, input Input) (*Output, error) {
    return &Output{Greeting: "Hello, " + input.Name + "!"}, nil
}

Attach middleware using rpc.DefineMiddlewares(rpc.M("auth", options)) in the FunctionConfig's Middlewares field. Actual credential verification belongs to that middleware. Use ctx.Set/Get or rpc.GetContext to consume validated state; remote HTTP/IPC payloads do not establish trusted context.

Register can infer object schemas from structs, but explicit native schemas are needed for precise non-object/nullable contracts. HTTP omission defaults to {}; explicit null reaches validation as nil. Input/output checks remain active.

Uploaded files use native methods: Filename(), Size(), MimeType(), Bytes(), Reader(), TempPath(), SaveTo(path). They are not exported struct fields. Persist to a unique application-owned destination during processing; temporary input files are cleaned afterward. Use native schema.File/Array rules and valid multipart routing; nested files are not a newly supported transport format.

FunctionMetadata.IsPublic remains a deprecated ignored bool compatibility field. It has no docs visibility, authorization, registration or execution effect. New generators omit it; no replacement flag exists.

docs.title: Public installation
docs.text:
Go>=1.27.4 is required. Module and CLI version v1.0.2 use the same versioned release:

go install github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go/cmd/crpc-go@v1.0.2
crpc-go version
crpc-go init my-api
cd my-api
go mod tidy
go build ./...
go test ./...
crpc-go dev

Put GOBIN, or the default Go bin directory, on PATH. The versioned installed CLI selects SDK v1.0.2 automatically. No parent checkout, replace directive or workspace is required for generated applications. For an existing module, use go get github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go@v1.0.2.

Local/VCS-stamped builds retain the older v1.0.0 fallback because a local Git revision may not identify published code. This is independent of the CLI's human-readable version. Use go work init . /absolute/path/to/rpc-go only for intentional local SDK development; keep machine-specific workspaces local. GOWORK=off selects the declared released dependency. The older v1.0.0 does not contain the v1.0.2 hardening fixes; prefer the versioned installed CLI for users.

docs.title: Generated layout and CLI
docs.text:
The app contains cmd/server/main.go, functions/user/getProfile and updateProfile, middlewares/auth, utilities, go.mod, Makefile and .env examples. Go functions register through init(); the server imports modules and calls UseGlobalRegistry. Add new module imports/registration deliberately; there is no filesystem function discovery or automatic TypeScript export CLI command in Go.

crpc-go create:function --ns user --name updateEmail
crpc-go create:function --ns user --name uploadAvatar --multipart
crpc-go create:middleware --name auth --desc 'Verify credentials'
crpc-go build

Use batch/file specs for generation where needed. Unlike Node's function CLI, Go has no --middlewares flag; edit the generated middleware attachments. The sample middleware is a no-op customization stub. Implement real verification before relying on auth; schema metadata does not do it for you.

docs.title: Environment and docs
docs.text:
Neither the generated binary nor crpc-go dev automatically loads .env. Export deployment values, or source the trusted shell-compatible generated file:

set -a
. ./.env
set +a
go run ./cmd/server

Final exported values win; sourcing replaces earlier exports, later exports replace sourced values. DOCS_ENABLED accepts trimmed case-insensitive true/false, 1/0 and Go t/f aliases. Unset/blank uses NODE_ENV != "production"; invalid nonblank values stop startup, including production. DOCS_PATH trims and defaults to /docs. Core programmatic DocsEnabled/DocsPath are separate and read no env.

The current generated listener still hard-codes 0.0.0.0:4000 and /rpc. Although the env example includes PORT/HOST/RPC_PATH, main does not consume them; edit rpc.Config explicitly when deploying on another address/path. No new env parser or listener feature is introduced by these docs.

Deprecated IsPublic is ignored; docs availability is global, independent of middleware/auth and function execution. See docs controls.

docs.title: Interactive Documentation Portal
docs.text: CellsWeb RPC Go features a built-in, server-rendered API documentation UI available at /docs. It requires zero third-party UI dependencies.

docs.title: 🎨 UI Features
docs.text:
• Dark Theme by Default: Clean, high-contrast dark aesthetic matching modern developer tools.
  • 2-Column Split Schema View:
  • Left Side: Human-readable recursive field tree (• user (object) -> • id (string, required)). Binary file uploads display cleanly as File / Binary.
  • Right Side: Formatted JSON Schema code block with a one-click Copy button.
  • Dynamic Middleware Cards:
  • Uses existing rpc.MiddlewareMetadata and native schema.SchemaRule schemas.
  • Properties & Controls: Lists schema-defined option names, types, descriptions, nested fields and required/optional status. Configured values and schema defaults are never displayed.
  • Required Headers: Distinguishes required and optional headers. Only required headers appear in function header tables and JSON/multipart cURL placeholders.
  • Ready-to-Run cURL Snippets: Auto-generates fully-formed cURL commands populated with mock payload data.
  • Instant Client Search: Fast search filter across all namespaces, functions, tags, and descriptions.

docs.title: ⚙️ Enabling & Configuring Docs
docs.text:
Configure the interactive docs when initializing CoreRPC:

app, err := rpc.New(rpc.Config{
    RpcPath:     "/rpc",
    DocsEnabled: os.Getenv("NODE_ENV") != "production", // Enable in dev / staging
    DocsPath:    "/docs",                              // Documentation portal URL
    CORS: &rpc.CorsConfig{
        AllowOrigins: []string{"*"},
    },
})

docs.title: 🧭 Navigating the Portal
docs.text:
1. Dashboard (/docs):
  2. Displays all registered functions grouped by namespace.
  3. Shows HTTP content types ([JSON] vs [FORM]).

  4. Links to the central middleware catalog.

  5. Function Detail View (/docs/:namespace/:functionName):

  6. Deep inspection of a single RPC function.
  7. 2-column input and output schema breakdowns.
  8. All attached middleware names, descriptions and schema contracts; no resolved runtime option values.

  9. Ready-to-copy cURL command.

  10. Middleware Catalog (/docs/middlewares/:name):

  11. Central catalog documenting all available middlewares.
  12. Detailed header and configuration schemas.

docs.title: Public documentation and private configuration
docs.text:
The UI never reads per-function middleware option values, including middleware without schemas. Middleware schema defaults are omitted recursively from the public JSON Schema projection. Types, descriptions, structural constraints and required fields remain visible; function input/output contracts keep their existing rendering. Keep secrets out of names, descriptions and other public schema metadata: the renderer cannot classify secrets deliberately placed in public prose or constraints.

Provide documentation using the existing registration API:

rpc.RegisterMiddleware("auth", "Checks bearer credentials", Run,
    schema.Object(map[string]*schema.SchemaRule{
        "roles": schema.Optional(schema.Array(schema.String())).Describe("Allowed roles"),
    }),
    schema.Object(map[string]*schema.SchemaRule{
        "authorization": schema.String().Describe("Bearer credentials"),
        "x-trace": schema.Optional(schema.String()).Describe("Optional trace identifier"),
    }),
)

This uses the existing schema abstractions; the documentation changes do not validate middleware options or headers at execution time, apply defaults, execute middleware, or change application handlers. Authentication and authorization remain the middleware's responsibility. Configured application values and the original schema objects remain unchanged.

Docs remain globally controlled by rpc.Config.DocsEnabled and DocsPath. Generated servers honor DOCS_ENABLED and DOCS_PATH with their existing exported environment behavior; see Getting Started. Disabling docs blocks their pages without changing registration or RPC execution.

docs.title: Deprecated metadata compatibility
docs.text: rpc.FunctionMetadata.IsPublic bool is deprecated and ignored. It controls neither documentation visibility nor authentication/authorization. Its type, field order and JSON tag are retained so existing struct literals, field reads and serialization keep working. Omitting it uses the existing zero value; false and true have identical framework behavior. PUBLIC/PRIVATE badges have been removed, and generators/examples no longer emit the field. No replacement visibility flag is introduced. Removal is reserved for a future major release. Node's optional FunctionMetadata.isPublic follows the same policy.

docs.title: Middleware and authentication
docs.text:
Go middleware receives (*rpc.Context, headers, options) and returns an error to stop processing. It runs before input validation and the handler. Store verified application state under a middleware-specific context key.

package auth

import (
    "strings"
    "github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go/pkg/rpc"
    "github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go/pkg/schema"
)
type Session struct { UserID, Role string }
// Application integration point; this example denies until it is implemented.
var VerifyToken = func(_ string) (Session, error) {
    return Session{}, rpc.NewError(rpc.ErrUnauthorized, "Configure credential verification")
}
func Run(ctx *rpc.Context, headers map[string]string, options map[string]any) error {
    raw := headers["authorization"]
    if !strings.HasPrefix(raw, "Bearer ") { return rpc.NewError(rpc.ErrUnauthorized, "Bearer credentials required") }
    session, err := VerifyToken(strings.TrimPrefix(raw, "Bearer "))
    if err != nil { return err }
    if session.UserID == "" { return rpc.NewError(rpc.ErrUnauthorized, "Invalid credentials") }
    role, _ := options["role"].(string)
    if role != "" && session.Role != role { return rpc.NewError(rpc.ErrForbidden, "Insufficient role") }
    ctx.Set("auth", session)
    return nil
}
func init() {
    rpc.RegisterMiddleware("auth", "Verify a bearer session and role", Run,
        schema.Object(map[string]*schema.SchemaRule{"role": schema.Optional(schema.String())}),
        schema.Object(map[string]*schema.SchemaRule{"authorization": schema.String().Describe("Bearer credentials")}),
    )
}

These option/header schemas are native documentation metadata. Go does not gain automatic middleware option/header validation from them; the application must validate its configuration and credentials. Node's middleware schema checks are different implementation semantics, while auth responsibility is shared.

Consume state with rpc.GetContext[auth.Session](ctx,"auth") after the matching middleware establishes it. Middleware namespacing organizes server-owned state; it is not a mechanism for accepting identity from caller JSON.

There is no supported remote middleware-skip/context-injection authentication workflow. Legacy Node IPC CallOptions fields named skipMiddlewares/context are retained/transmitted for compatibility, but the Go bridge ignores them and always uses the middleware pipeline. Forward credentials through headers instead.

Generated middleware is an editable no-op stub, not production authentication. Docs show structural options/header schemas, descriptions and required status; they do not read live configured options/defaults. IsPublic is deprecated and ignored; it cannot grant or deny execution.

docs.title: Release and migration
docs.text:
Version v1.0.2 adds the stdio frame-limit correction to the earlier hardening/documentation fixes. The historical v1.0.0 tag predates these changes and remains unchanged. Use Go>=1.27.4 and install the exact versioned CLI/module as described in installation.

Installed versioned CLIs generate matching SDK requirements. Source/VCS builds still use the older v1.0.0 fallback; a display version is not a dependency pin. Use an explicit workspace only to select a local SDK checkout deliberately. Preserve the migration considerations below when updating an existing app.

Explicit HTTP data:null reaches schema validation/handlers as nil; omission still defaults to {}. Arrays/scalars stay intact. CallInMemory/CallRaw/Unix IPC accept the same JSON shapes subject to native schemas. These are not new output-null, large-integer or JSON Schema keyword guarantees. HTTP 200 application errors stay the default; standard status mapping remains opt-in.

IsPublic is retained as a deprecated ignored bool. Remove it from new metadata; there are no badges or replacement flags. Docs availability is global and never changes authentication. Middleware owns verified state for HTTP/in-memory/IPC; legacy remote skip/context fields are ignored, not security features.

Unix frames are bounded 2,097,152 bytes. Node client socket-close/anonymous errors and malformed response JSON reject pending callers promptly, clean resources and retire the affected connection. Later calls can reconnect without replaying work.

Generated servers honor exported DOCS_ENABLED/DOCS_PATH but do not load .env. Keep local workspaces out of portable production setup. The Node releases are core 1.0.35/client 1.0.26/scaffolder 1.0.31 (documentation-only patches; runtime unchanged from core1.0.34/client1.0.25/scaffolder1.0.30), declare Node>=24.0.0 and preserve Bun support. Its union fix restores strict nullable/file validation; native schema vocabularies still differ. Review both changelogs before deployment.

docs.title: Go Unix IPC and Node
docs.text:
Use the maintained example-node/src/client.ts and generated contract types in this repository rather than copying another client implementation into guides. The client has connection-generation tracking, pending timer cleanup, concurrent call correlation and tested failure/reconnection behavior.

HTTP middleware/auth rules remain in force over IPC. Forward credentials through headers. Legacy CallOptions skipMiddlewares/context fields remain for source/wire compatibility but are ignored by the Go bridge; they do not skip checks or inject trusted identity. Do not use an SSR session object as a remote auth bypass.

package main

import (
    "log"
    _ "docsexamples/functions/hello"
    "github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go/pkg/rpc"
    "github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go/pkg/nodebridge"
)
func main() {
    app, err := rpc.New(rpc.Config{RpcPath:"/rpc", CORS:&rpc.CorsConfig{AllowOrigins:[]string{"*"}}})
    if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
    app.UseGlobalRegistry()
    if err := nodebridge.ServeUnixSocket(app, "/tmp/crpc-example.sock"); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
}

import { GoRpcClient, RpcError } from './src/client.js';
export async function profile(token: string) {
  const client = new GoRpcClient({ socketPath: '/tmp/crpc.sock' });
  try {
    return await client.call('user.getProfile', { id: 'user-1' },
      { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }, timeoutMs: 5000 });
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof RpcError) console.error(error.code, error.message);
    throw error;
  } finally { client.close(); }
}

Copy the maintained client and matching crpc.d.ts as a unit; this example's user.getProfile contract must actually be registered in your daemon. Regenerate types from your own app: call nodebridge.GenerateTypeScriptDeclarations(app.Functions()) and write its returned string. No crpc-go export:types command exists. File uploads use HTTP multipart; the JSON IPC client does not transport live File/Blob objects just because a generated HTTP-oriented type mentions them.

Unix requests support newline JSON or four-byte big-endian length framing. The maximum is 2,097,152 bytes; newline counts for line frames, prefix is separate for length frames. ServeStdio is newline-only with the same line-frame maximum, including LF/CRLF, and retains acceptance of a final line at EOF. It returns bufio.ErrTooLong on oversized input; the Unix connection error/deadline behavior described below is separate from stdio's parent-owned process lifecycle. Socket files use 0600 permissions; select an application-owned directory/path.

The Node client uses JSON-Lines responses. Socket closure, anonymous connection errors and malformed response JSON promptly reject affected pending calls with network_error and retire the connection. Later calls may reconnect; failed calls are never automatically replayed and there is no automatic background backoff loop. Matched valid application errors, ordinary timeouts and request IDs retain their existing behavior. Some syntactically valid invalid envelopes are ignored; do not claim a new wire-level validation convention.

IPC errors use the bridge's id/status/error envelope, not an invented HTTP error wire format. Shared success data/validation/auth semantics do not imply every HTTP/IPC code/details/output-omission field is identical. Test nil outputs and generated contracts for your app. No universal 20–50µs latency guarantee applies.

docs.title: Native schemas
docs.text:
Use schema.SchemaRule builders or FromStruct for object contracts. These native rules overlap with TypeBox but are not an implementation of every JSON Schema keyword or union. Keep shared logical conformance tests for the contracts used.

package schemas

import "github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go/pkg/schema"

var Submission = schema.Object(map[string]*schema.SchemaRule{
    "title":  schema.String().Min(1).Max(100),
    "score":  schema.Number().MinValue(0.0),
    "count":  schema.Integer().MinValue(0),
    "active": schema.Boolean(),
    "avatar": schema.Optional(schema.File().MaxSize(5 * 1024 * 1024).AllowedMimes("image/png")),
})

var Profile = schema.Object(map[string]*schema.SchemaRule{
    "name":   schema.String().Min(1).Max(100).Describe("Display name"),
    "age":    schema.Optional(schema.Integer().MinValue(0)),
    "avatar": schema.Optional(schema.File().MaxSize(5 * 1024 * 1024).AllowedMimes("image/png")),
})
var NullableText = schema.Optional(schema.String())
var Names = schema.Array(schema.String())

docs.title: Optional and Nullable Contracts
docs.text: Native Optional allows nil. This does not change HTTP omission: omitted data is an empty object, so a nullable string schema rejects it. Explicit null is nil and can be accepted. Object property absence/nil and output omission are separate contracts; test typed pointers/omitempty explicitly where they matter.

docs.title: Schema Builders and Struct Inference
docs.text: FromStruct reads json names/omitempty, doc/description, min/max, min_files/max_files, max_size, and mimes tags. Use explicit builders (schema.String(), schema.Number(), schema.Integer(), schema.Boolean(), schema.File()) for precise non-object or numeric constraints. Defaults stored in schema metadata are not an automatic application-default engine. Input/output validation remains enforced; middleware option/header schemas are documentation metadata and do not add pipeline checks.

docs.title: Schema-Directed Multipart Coercion
docs.text:
In multipart requests (multipart/form-data), all form fields arrive over HTTP framing as raw text strings. Unlike Node (which uses explicit FormNum() / FormBool() wrapper schemas), Go provides automatic schema-directed multipart coercion during transport intake (schema.CoerceMultipartData).

Before input validation runs on a multipart request, the engine traverses the declared InputSchema and automatically converts string form fields into native types matching the schema:

Schema Rule FormData Input Coerced Value & Handler Type schema.String() "42" string "42" (remains a string) schema.Number() "42" float64 42.0 (numeric) schema.Integer() "42" int64 42 (integer) schema.Boolean() "true" or "1" bool true schema.Boolean() "false" or "0" bool false

docs.title: String Retention vs Numeric Coercion
docs.text: Because coercion is strictly schema-directed: - A field declared as schema.String() receives the raw string "42". - The exact same input "42" under schema.Number() or schema.Integer() is automatically parsed into a float64 or int64 before the handler receives it. - Coercion applies recursively through nested objects and multi-dimensional arrays declared in the schema.

docs.title: Accepted Boolean Strings
docs.text:
For schema.Boolean(), multipart intake accepts: - "true" and "1" (case-insensitive and trimmed) -> coerced to true - "false" and "0" (case-insensitive and trimmed) -> coerced to false

Any unrecognized string (e.g. "invalid", "yes", "off") cannot be parsed as a boolean, remains a string, and consequently fails boolean schema validation.

docs.title: Strict JSON Validation Remains Enforced
docs.text: Schema-directed coercion is strictly confined to multipart transport intake. Normal JSON requests (Content-Type: application/json) remain strictly validated: - In JSON requests, passing a string "42" for a field declared with schema.Number() or schema.Integer() is rejected with a validation error. - JSON payloads must match their declared native JSON types directly without transport coercion.

docs.title: Validation Errors and HTTP 200 Contract
docs.text:
When an invalid value is provided (e.g. "abc" for schema.Number(), "invalid" for schema.Boolean(), or a numeric constraint violation), validation fails before handler invocation.

Under the framework's uniform architecture, handled application errors return HTTP 200 OK by default with an RPC error envelope:

{
  "status": "error",
  "code": "validation_error",
  "message": "validation failed",
  "details": [
    {
      "path": "score",
      "message": "expected number, got string"
    }
  ]
}

The raw HTTP status remains 200 OK by default; transport/framing failures are distinct from handled application validation errors. Applications requiring conventional HTTP error statuses can optionally enable UseHttpStatusCodes: true in rpc.Config.

docs.title: General Guidelines
docs.text: Go objects reject fields absent from their Properties contract. HTTP JSON v2 rejects duplicate members; IPC/in-memory use existing JSON decoding conventions. Do not assume identical large-integer precision or every keyword across Node/Go. File MIME detection/limits do not sanitize the content itself.

docs.title: Report privately
docs.text:
Please report suspected vulnerabilities through GitHub private vulnerability reporting when the repository's Security tab offers Report a vulnerability. Availability is a repository setting; opening a public issue is not a fallback for sensitive reports.

If the private form is unavailable, use info@cellsweb.com or the official contact page to request a private reporting channel. Send only a brief nonsensitive request until a suitable channel is confirmed. Do not post exploit details in public issues, discussions, pull requests, logs or chat transcripts.

docs.title: What to include in a private report
docs.text:
• Affected repository, package/module version, runtime and operating system.
  • A minimal reproducible example, prerequisites and expected/actual behavior.
  • Security impact and the trust boundary crossed; identify HTTP, multipart, in-memory or IPC paths and whether authentication is required.
  • Relevant sanitized requests/responses and the earliest known affected version. Use dummy credentials and files, not customer data, keys or production secrets.

Allow maintainers to reproduce and coordinate a fix before public disclosure. Discuss disclosure timing privately; this policy does not promise an invented acknowledgment deadline or backport schedule. Maintainers will determine affected versions and release guidance during triage.

docs.title: Release context and responsibilities
docs.text:
The release-line installation guides and changelogs identify package/module versions. Include your exact installed versions when reporting, including older versions if relevant. There is no published long-term-support matrix here.

Application middleware owns credential verification and authorization. Generated auth modules are customization examples. Deprecated isPublic/IsPublic metadata is ignored, and docs availability is globally configured. These facts do not exclude genuine framework bypasses, data exposure or resource-exhaustion reports.

For ordinary nonsensitive bugs use the bug template. Conduct concerns follow the Code of Conduct.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
CallInMemory and TestCaller run without an HTTP socket, through middleware and schema checks. They are not transport tests and do not bypass authorization. Call unwraps data/errors; CallRaw returns an envelope plus its helper error. An application error can be in that envelope even when the Go error return is nil.

package testing_test

import (
    "testing"
    _ "docsexamples/functions/hello"
    "github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go/pkg/rpc"
)
func TestHello(t *testing.T) {
    app, err := rpc.New(rpc.Config{RpcPath: "/rpc", CORS: &rpc.CorsConfig{AllowOrigins: []string{"*"}}})
    if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
    app.UseGlobalRegistry()
    caller := rpc.NewTestCaller(app)
    response, err := caller.CallRaw("public.hello", map[string]any{"name":"Test"})
    if err != nil || response == nil || response.Status != "ok" { t.Fatalf("%+v %v", response, err) }
    response, err = caller.CallRaw("public.hello", map[string]any{"name":123})
    if err != nil || response == nil || response.Code != rpc.ErrValidation { t.Fatalf("%+v %v", response, err) }
}

Both helpers support objects, arrays, scalars and nil subject to schemas. Return types differ: CallInMemory populates your output target; CallRaw exposes protocol metadata. Use Headers in CallOptions/TestOptions to supply valid test credentials; do not inject unverified identity to make authorization tests pass.

Release checks: go build, full go test, race detector, vet, real HTTP multipart/ docs tests and Node IPC tests. Enable CRPC_STANDALONE_INTEGRATION=1 for actual public-module scaffold resolution; enable CRPC_SCAFFOLD_RACE=1 to instrument generated child binaries. Those integration cases require a public proxy/cache and an unused port 4000. Node example tests use actual Go IPC daemons and optional CRPC_IPC_TEST_RACE=1, covering disconnect/corruption/reconnect without replay.

docs.title: Go architecture and source map
docs.text:
Read shared contracts and the request lifecycle before changing a subsystem. This describes the released native implementation; it does not propose a common pipeline or new schema API.
