Its presence is not proof of a configured external S3 integration. The imagehandler helper uses UploadedFile.Bytes and the engine to replace/store image references; its name does not imply an image-resizing or content-sanitization pipeline. storage_test.go covers the storage boundary separately from RPC parser cleanup. example, example-mongo and benchmarks contain nested modules; root tests do not traverse them. The Go module has the actual dependencies listed in go.mod; do not claim it has no dependency beyond one library by copying an old review summary.

There is no shared executePipeline helper or general TypeBox union interpreter. rpc.Context is framework state, not a stdlib context.Context cancellation contract. HTTP JSON, HTTP multipart, CallInMemory and CallRaw have separate implementations and observable differences. Read the validation matrix before assuming a change to one path covers all others.

Continue with registration/context, transport/uploads, IPC lifecycle, docs renderer, CLI, testing and release engineering. The sibling Node internals uses TypeBox and filesystem discovery instead of mirroring this implementation.

docs.title: Unix/stdio bridge and Node client lifecycle
docs.text: Source: pkg/nodebridge/bridge.go, example-node/src/client.ts and pkg/nodebridge/ts_gen.go. The Node HTTP SDK and this example Unix client are different clients; do not mix their envelopes or file support.

docs.title: Wire shape and dispatch
docs.text: BridgeRequest has id, function, data and optional headers. Function is the combined key. Both bridge paths call CallInMemory with supplied headers and an output target; no remote skipMiddlewares/context values populate trusted Context. BridgeResponse has id/status and optional data/error/details. The bridge currently returns an error string rather than the complete HTTP code/meta envelope. Its data omitempty means nil output may omit data; explicit input null preservation is a separate guarantee. Type declarations are generated from app.Functions(), not Node filesystem discovery.

docs.title: Unix framing and daemon ownership
docs.text:
ServeUnixSocket prepares a parent directory, refuses to replace non-socket paths, removes an old socket path, binds and chmods the socket 0600. Its listener/socket cleanup is deferred when the function returns; abrupt process death may leave a socket path for the next startup to inspect. Use an application-owned location and supervisor policy. HTTP app shutdown does not imply this separate listener has a stop handle.

Each accepted connection gets a goroutine; within that connection, the loop reads one frame, executes CallInMemory and writes a response before reading the next. The client can have several pending IDs, but this server loop does not launch a new goroutine for every frame on that same connection.

  • First-byte '{' selects newline JSON; otherwise the reader expects a4-byte big-endian length prefix. Emit compact object lines as the Node client does; do not assume arbitrary leading whitespace selects newline mode.
  • MaxIPCFrameSize is 2,097,152 bytes. Newline counts in the line limit; the four-byte prefix is separate from the length-framed payload maximum.
  • readLineFrame uses buffered fragments and at most a capped overflow buffer, rejecting oversized/no-newline streams before unlimited allocation.
  • Read deadlines are reset to60s for each frame; write deadlines are30s. Partial EOF/deadline/frame errors retire the connection. Valid framing with malformed request JSON yields an anonymous error and can continue at the next frame.
  • Responses are JSON-Lines for both accepted request framing modes.

ServeStdio uses bufio.Scanner with the same 2,097,152-byte line-frame limit, including LF or CRLF delimiters. One bounded lookahead byte distinguishes an exact-limit final EOF line from overflow; it does not increase the frame limit. Scanner retains its existing blank-line/CRLF handling and accepts a final line without a newline at EOF, unlike Unix framing. Oversized input returns bufio.ErrTooLong and stops serving without a response envelope; the parent owns process shutdown. Malformed JSON within the limit returns an anonymous error and can continue at the next line. Stdio does not accept Unix length-prefixed frames.

docs.title: Client connection generations and pending requests
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Application
  participant C as GoRpcClient
  participant S as Unix socket
  participant G as Go bridge
  A->>C: call(function, data, headers)
  C->>S: Connect once / allocate UUID and timer
  S->>G: JSON line
  G->>G: CallInMemory with middleware and schemas
  G-->>C: ID-correlated JSON line
  C->>C: Delete pending ID / clear timer
  C-->>A: Resolve data or reject RpcError
  opt Socket close / anonymous error / corrupt response
    C->>C: Retire generation / detach listeners / reject all pending
    C-->>A: network_error, no replay
  end

connect coalesces simultaneous connection attempts and ties event handlers to the owning socket generation. settleRequest removes the ID before clearing its timer and resolving/rejecting, so late replies cannot double-settle it. disconnect closes readline/socket resources, clears the current generation and rejects all its pending callers. Older socket events cannot retire a newer connection.

Malformed response JSON is stream corruption: reject affected pending calls and retire that socket. Anonymous id:""/missing-ID error envelopes are connection- level failures, not an error assigned arbitrarily to one request. Ordinary valid matched errors remain RPC errors, timeouts settle the matching request and later calls can reconnect. Failed calls are never automatically replayed. Some syntactically valid non-envelope/unmatched responses are ignored by the current parser; do not claim universal envelope validation or new wire conventions.

Use the public IPC usage guide, build the maintained client and matching crpc.d.ts together, and inspect real-daemon/fault-proxy tests in the testing map. IPC transports JSON, not live HTTP File/Blob objects.

docs.title: Go request execution lifecycle
docs.text: Source: pkg/rpc/engine.go, pkg/rpc/context.go and pkg/rpc/handler.go. CoreRPC owns app maps/config/server, while Context is per-request state.

docs.title: HTTP entry and routing
docs.text:
Handler returns the fasthttp callback. It handles OPTIONS/CORS first, then custom HTTP routes, enabled docs, POST at RpcPath, and unmatched404. Custom HTTP routes precede RPC/docs matching and have their own behavior; they do not automatically execute function middleware. NetHTTPHandler wraps the request body in a configured MaxBytesReader then adapts to the same fasthttp handler. Listen/Serve configure body/time limits; a plain Handler used by another host depends on that host too.

sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant H as CoreRPC.Handler
  participant J as handleJsonRPC
  participant M as Attached middleware
  participant V as schema.Validate
  participant F as Typed Handler wrapper
  C->>H: POST RpcPath
  H->>J: handleRpcRequest / NewContext
  J->>J: Parse envelope, preserve null/omission
  J->>J: Resolve registered function
  J->>M: Headers + options + Context
  M-->>J: Error or trusted state
  J->>V: Validate input
  J->>F: Raw data + Context
  F->>F: Adapt input / inject files / call user function
  F-->>J: Result or error
  J->>V: Validate non-nil output when schema exists
  J-->>C: HTTP envelope
  H->>H: Deferred Context.Cleanup

docs.title: JSON path
docs.text:
handleRpcRequest creates Context with request ID, headers/IP and deferred cleanup. It dispatches by Content-Type to JSON or multipart; unsupported kinds become handled RPC errors. handleJsonRPC uses encoding/json/v2 for the envelope. A pointer sentinel distinguishes absent data (empty object) from explicit null (nil). Routing is trimmed/validated and FormatFunctionKey selects an app entry.

Attachments are resolved and invoked in order; a missing middleware fails closed. Input goes through native schema.Validate. Handler invokes either the registered raw callback or Register's generic adapter. Successful non-nil output is checked when an output schema exists, then sendSuccessResponse serializes it. Validation and middleware/handler errors go through sendErrorResponse/dispatchError.

docs.title: Multipart and in-memory differences
docs.text:
Multipart chooses paired header routing or ParseMultipartPhase1, runs middleware before Phase2 application file writes, tracks created files, checks header/body consistency, applies schema-directed multipart coercion and validates input. It then executes/validates output similarly. Native fasthttp has already buffered the request; early application authorization is not a zero-network-buffer guarantee.

CallInMemory creates its own Context and runs a separate chain. Non-nil maps keep native values; other inputs marshal/unmarshal as arbitrary JSON shapes. It returns an error and fills a caller-supplied output target. CallRaw uses another chain and returns a ResponseEnvelope; it currently does not run the production output-schema check. These paths are not aliases of one internal executePipeline method. See validation and IPC before editing shared behavior.

docs.title: Error/telemetry and resource boundaries
docs.text:
sendErrorResponse defaults to HTTP200; UseHttpStatusCodes invokes the explicit mapper. Errors from malformed JSON, invalid routing and similar handled cases also use that default, contrary to a blanket400 claim. fasthttp body/parser errors, custom route errors and unmatched paths can occur outside the RPC wrapper. Meta requestId/durationMs is produced by each path; the IPC response is a different envelope and does not promise all HTTP fields.

HTTP request cleanup is deferred by handleRpcRequest; partial upload creation errors clean files inside the multipart parser before ownership transfers to Context. Copy files to application-owned storage while the request is alive. Do not retain pooled fasthttp RequestCtx buffers or raw Context after response. Config's read/write/idle deadlines bound transport operation, not arbitrary CPU handler work. No implicit client failure replay or new cancellation API exists.

When extending behavior, enumerate HTTP JSON, multipart, CallInMemory, CallRaw and bridge effects explicitly. A passing test for one is not coverage for all four separate execution sites. Use the test map, not an incidental refactor.

docs.title: Shared protocol and compatibility boundaries
docs.text: This is a contributor description of the released behavior, not a new wire specification. Use it with the sibling runtime's source and equivalent fixtures. Node and Go share semantic contracts while retaining different native APIs, parsers, schema vocabularies and response details.

docs.title: HTTP envelope
docs.text:
A configurable endpoint (normally POST /rpc) receives an object with namespace, functionName and data. The outer JSON value is an envelope object; the data member may be an object, array, string, number, boolean or null if its schema accepts it. Omitted HTTP data retains the empty-object default; explicit null must reach schema validation as null/nil. Do not conflate envelope shape with handler-input shape.

{"namespace":"public","functionName":"hello","data":{"name":"Ada"}}

Success normally carries status:"ok", data and optional metadata. Some Go paths omit nil output data under existing omitempty rules; explicit null input is a separate guarantee. Errors have status:"error", code, message and optional details/metadata. Successfully handled application errors use HTTP200 by default, with explicit opt-in HTTP status mapping. Framework/server framing errors, custom routes and unmatched paths may instead use transport statuses or different non-RPC bodies.

Both interceptors in Node and sendErrorResponse in Go send their handled parsing errors through the default HTTP200 path too. Do not claim all malformed JSON, routing conflicts or missing boundaries automatically become HTTP400. Inspect which layer produced the failure, plus its configuration. Clients inspect the RPC status field instead of treating HTTP200 alone as success.

docs.title: Authentication, context and docs
docs.text:
Application middleware verifies credentials and authorization, in attachment order, before the handler. Missing configured middleware fails closed. HTTP/IPC callers forward headers; body/session/context objects remain untrusted data. Server-local test/context APIs are not remote bypass controls.

isPublic/IsPublic are deprecated ignored compatibility fields. They neither register/hide functions nor bypass authorization. No replacement visibility flag exists. Documentation is enabled/disabled globally. Middleware docs project structural schemas, descriptions and required headers, not resolved secret values. Never place secrets in public prose, names or schema constraints.

docs.title: Multipart is a transport, not a second business API
docs.text:
The client emits namespace/functionName text parts before files and also sends X-CRPC-Namespace/X-CRPC-Function. Header routing is an acceleration; required body routing is redundant and must agree. Headers come as a pair. Reject duplicates and conflicts rather than selecting an arbitrary source. Headerless fallback requires routing fields before file parts. Required authorization precedes application-owned file writes; this does not imply zero socket/runtime buffering.

File inputs are top-level fields or direct arrays of files. Nested files inside objects are not supported by the shared client transport. Ordinary nested JSON is separate. Text fields may be schema-coerced during multipart intake; ordinary JSON does not receive blanket transport coercion. Preserve parser/schema bounds, abort handling and temporary-file ownership.

docs.title: Shared intent and deliberate differences
docs.text:
Boundary Contributor implication Node discovery / Go registration Do not add filesystem discovery to Go to mimic Node. TypeBox / native SchemaRule Compare logical valid/invalid cases, not schema syntax. Optional/null/default semantics are not universally identical. Native Node / Fetch / Go HTTP Stream-driven Busboy, runtime-buffered formData, and transport-buffered fasthttp have different resource bounds. HTTP / in-memory / IPC HTTP omission defaults are not a promise about missing input on every call API. Return types and error/details/meta differ. Unix / stdio IPC Both bound line frames to 2,097,152 bytes including delimiters. Unix additionally accepts length-prefixed requests; stdio retains Scanner's final-EOF-line behavior. Browser / RN / Node client Client1.0.25 web FormData uses fetchFn; native getParts-compatible FormData retains XHR when available. Earlier clients select XHR whenever present.

Large integers, JSON duplicate members, extra properties, null outputs/omitempty, Unicode limits, details fields and cancellation need explicit fixtures when changed. Do not infer universal JSON Schema or byte-for-byte response parity. For protocol changes, propose version/migration behavior first and test both runtimes and every affected transport before seeking review.

See Node internals and Go internals.

docs.title: Go registration, typed handlers and context
docs.text: Source: pkg/rpc/registry.go, pkg/rpc/handler.go and pkg/rpc/context.go.

docs.title: Global versus app registration
docs.text:
Package-level RegisterFunction/RegisterMiddleware populate global maps protected by globalMu. Generic Register builds a FunctionDefinition and registers it globally. UseGlobalRegistry copies entries into a CoreRPC instance; import the function and middleware packages before calling it. A package existing on disk does not run its init function and changes after a copy do not automatically update that app.

App.RegisterFunction/RegisterMiddleware register directly on an instance. Normal setup completes registration before serving; do not infer safe live mutation of all registry reads just because registration methods use locks. FormatFunctionKey trims components and joins namespace/function; HTTP route validation remains a separate boundary. SplitFunctionKey separates at the final dot for IPC/codegen.

flowchart TD
  I["Application imports packages"] --> Init["init calls Register / RegisterMiddleware"]
  Init --> Global["Global registry maps"]
  Global --> Copy["app.UseGlobalRegistry"]
  Direct["app.RegisterFunction / RegisterMiddleware"] --> Maps["App maps"]
  Copy --> Maps
  Maps --> HTTP["HTTP dispatch"]
  Maps --> Memory["CallInMemory / CallRaw"]
  Maps --> Docs["Docs / declaration generator"]

docs.title: Typed wrapper
docs.text:
FunctionConfig includes namespace/name/content type, metadata, schemas, middleware attachments and a Handler(ctx,input) returning *Output,error. Register infers schemas with FromStruct when explicit schemas are absent. For precise non-object contracts supply native rules deliberately; inference is not an arbitrary JSON Schema/TypeBox importer.

The wrapper JSON-adapts non-nil raw input into TInput, injects top-level UploadedFile pointers/direct file slices from native maps, then calls the user handler. Preserve native maps containing files until that injection point. A successful JSON round trip of a file placeholder is not evidence the live file instance survived.

docs.title: Middleware and Context
docs.text:
DefineMiddlewares/M express ordered attachments. RegisteredMiddleware contains a handler and native metadata schemas for options/headers. Those metadata schemas do not automatically validate headers/options at execution time. Middleware must verify the fields it needs, authenticate credentials and authorize access. It can use ctx.Set and typed GetContext to establish/retrieve trusted state.

Context owns a synchronized key/value store, request identity, normalized headers, client IP/path and tracked files. Header/Headers are request data, not identity. TrustProxy controls forwarded IP handling; review deployment trust explicitly. Raw returns the request context only where a live HTTP request exists; in-memory and IPC callers must not depend on HTTP-only fields.

Uploaded files tracked by HTTP Context are cleaned after request handling. SaveTo writes a distinct application-owned destination; it does not make a temporary path permanent. Background work must not retain request-owned resources blindly.

docs.title: Compatibility rules
docs.text:
Remote bridge fields named skipMiddlewares/context are legacy ignored values, not inputs to Context.Set. IsPublic is retained/deprecated/ignored and influences no auth, registration or docs visibility. Metadata changes should not run new runtime validation or execute user handlers when rendering docs.

Registration/wrapper/context changes need typed/raw input fixtures, middleware order/authorization, missing middleware, output errors and actual HTTP/IPC tests. The test map identifies exact files and API differences; do not add Node-style filesystem discovery as a contributor convenience.

docs.title: Release engineering and compatibility review
docs.text: Current documentation patch versions are Node core1.0.35/client1.0.26/scaffolder1.0.31, with runtime code/exports/dependencies unchanged from core1.0.34/client1.0.25/scaffolder1.0.30. Go module/CLI remains v1.0.2. The earlier client1.0.25 and Go v1.0.2 corrections are already publicly released; they must not be described as unpublished. Contributing a PR does not authorize pushing, tagging or publishing. Every release still requires author approval, validation and actual public-registry verification.

docs.title: Version and artifact boundaries
docs.text:
Node has three public npm workspaces plus a private root. Core runtime/helpers, client/React exports and the initializer have separate versions. Generated Node apps currently require core^1.0.34, so a new scaffolder must never require a core version that has not been published. Check actual registry state, not just local package manifests or a changed version string. Stable ranges do not select an unrelated prerelease; prerelease testing needs explicit versions/ranges/dist-tags.

Go is one root module, github.com/CellsWeb/crpc-go. Root tags select both SDK and cmd/crpc-go; no separate invented CLI tag is needed. An installed versioned CLI uses its module version for the generated dependency. Source/VCS builds still use the real older v1.0.0 fallback; select a local SDK explicitly with a workspace. A CLI printing1.0.2 is not by itself evidence of generated SDK selection.

docs.title: Review and integration gates
docs.text:
• Agree scope/version/migration policy before changing public APIs, defaults or wire behavior. Preserve the shared invariants and test both runtimes when affected.
  • Record baseline/new SHAs and exact red/green commands. Run runtime-specific full builds/tests/typechecks/vet/race and real adapter/IPC tests where applicable.
  • Review docs examples, configuration precedence, ignored legacy metadata, error envelopes and resource ownership. Test actual package declarations/executables.
  • Use a clean worktree to preserve unrelated edits. Refresh default/upstream refs, confirm ancestry and integrate only the approved commit. Never force history or overwrite a published version/tag to rescue a failed release.

docs.title: Distribution sequence
docs.text:
1. After explicit release approval, recheck registry/tag absence, credentials, package names, engines/dependencies/exports/bins and exact artifacts. npm pack --dry-run and an inspected actual pack are separate from publishing.
  2. Publish the new core before any scaffolder requiring its new range, and publish the client at its own approved version. Use the official public registry and required public access. Prefer browser authentication; the maintainer completes passkey/2FA personally. Never ask for credentials in a PR or report.
  3. Create the approved new Go root-module tag at the verified commit; check the public proxy/checksum database before advertising its matching CLI/SDK install. Keep one publishing operation at a time and inspect each actual result.
  4. Repeat real installs in independent projects with fresh public caches and no local SDK links/replacements/workspaces/tarball overrides. Generate with npm create cellsweb-rpc-api@latest or a pinned initializer; build/typecheck/test and send actual JSON/multipart/error/docs HTTP requests on all seven adapters.
  5. Install the exact public Go CLI, generate an app, verify its go.mod and go list -m version, build/test/run HTTP and check IPC with the maintained Node client. Do not silently fall back to older code when propagation is delayed.
  6. Record published versions, integrity/module sums, remote SHAs/tag target and actual public-install results. Only then describe distribution as complete.

Both existing GitHub Pages workflows deploy docs on relevant main pushes. Review that timing and published-status prose; changing MkDocs source does not update an already-published immutable npm tarball's bundled README. No CI/workflow changes are implied by this guide. User installation examples are in getting started; migration keeps useful history from v1.0.0/older npm versions without calling released artifacts unpublished.

docs.title: Go embedded docs renderer
docs.text: Source: pkg/rpc/docs.go with native schema export in pkg/schema/jsonschema.go. This is the runtime /docs feature, separate from the MkDocs contributor site.

docs.title: Routing and views
docs.text:
CoreRPC.Handler checks global DocsEnabled before handleDocsRequest. DocsPath is normalized; the request path chooses index, middleware detail or function detail. Known details render schemas and function-level middleware. Unknown documentation routes return a docs404 page in Go; Node's renderer currently falls back to its index. Preserve this existing difference unless deliberately reviewed.

renderDocsIndex/buildSidebar/renderFunctionDocs/renderMiddlewareDoc use function and middleware metadata to build descriptions, schema trees, required-header information and placeholder request/cURL examples. DocsPath and RpcPath flow into navigation and examples; custom paths must not become hard-coded /docs links. Descriptions and schemas are documentation, not invocation or authorization.

docs.title: Middleware metadata projection
docs.text:
MiddlewareMetadata.Options/Headers are native SchemaRule trees. The renderer recursively copies a safe structural projection using middlewareSchemaForDocs, excluding value/default annotations and preserving types/descriptions/constraints/ requiredness. Configured per-function option maps are not read/rendered as values. Projection must leave original schema objects and application configuration intact. Required headers follow the schema's required list and optional rules; cURL uses placeholders, not actual credentials. Nested options need recursive structure.

No middleware/handler executes when rendering docs. Adding metadata must not add runtime middleware validation or defaults. Function input/output rendering is separate from the stricter middleware projection. Keep secrets out of public names/descriptions/constraints; no heuristic redaction can classify all prose.

docs.title: Global controls and retained metadata
docs.text:
Core Config.DocsEnabled/DocsPath read no environment automatically. The generated main honors exported DOCS_ENABLED/DOCS_PATH with the documented production default and boolean validation; it does not automatically load.env. Raw programmatic zero DocsEnabled is false. Node generated/raw-core controls differ; preserve actual APIs rather than inventing a common visibility flag.

FunctionMetadata.IsPublic bool and Node isPublic remain deprecated/ignored. True, false and omitted values do not affect docs visibility, registration or execution. There are no PUBLIC/PRIVATE badges or per-function HideFromDocs behavior.

docs.title: Test before changing a view
docs.text: Use pkg/rpc/docs_parity_test.go for safe projection, ignored metadata, required headers and function middleware. Use pkg/rpc/docs_parity_http_test.go for actual fasthttp/net-http content, custom paths, docs disabled and execution independence. docs_test.go covers the complete renderer. Compare Node HTML/schema semantics without requiring identical styling or overriding intentional unknown-route behavior. The Node renderer guide links its Fetch/native path routing tests.

docs.title: Go test architecture and safe extension
docs.text:
Choose the layer that owns the behavior; do not assume all invocation paths share one implementation. The validation matrix documents return/output check differences that tests need to preserve or deliberately version.

Subsystem Real test file Relevant coverage HTTP engine/config pkg/rpc/engine_test.go Routing headers, middleware, transport status opt-in, telemetry/CORS HTTP JSON shapes pkg/rpc/http_json_shapes_test.go, pkg/rpc/testdata/http-json-shapes.json Missing data versus null, arbitrary shapes, schemas, auth, both HTTP handlers CallInMemory pkg/rpc/caller_test.go Native/typed shapes, validation and middleware CallRaw pkg/rpc/testing_test.go Shape parity, typed input, validation/auth/options and Go error-versus-envelope returns Multipart/files pkg/rpc/multipart_test.go File limits, primitive/array coercion, field sanitization and cleanup Custom HTTP routes pkg/rpc/http_routes_test.go Route precedence/helpers/internal calls Native schemas pkg/schema/schema_test.go Native rule types, struct JSON representation, files/limits Embedded docs pkg/rpc/docs_test.go, pkg/rpc/docs_parity_test.go, pkg/rpc/docs_parity_http_test.go Actual content, safe projection, required headers, custom/global docs and no execution Unix framing pkg/nodebridge/bridge_test.go Size allocation boundary, exact limit, no-newline/partial/malformed/deadline behavior and compatibility Generated declarations pkg/nodebridge/ts_gen_test.go Native schema-to-TypeScript mapping Generated apps cmd/crpc-go/commands/init_test.go, cmd/crpc-go/commands/init_module_test.go, cmd/crpc-go/commands/init_standalone_test.go Real executable/env/docs, version selection, public resolution and explicit workspace Node IPC client example-node/test/client.test.mjs, example-node/test/corruption.test.mjs, example-node/test/go-interop.test.mjs Mock sockets plus actual daemon, close/corruption/anonymous errors, IDs/timers/reconnect/no replay

The actual daemon fixture is example-node/test/testdata/ipc-daemon.go; it is testdata, not a production-discovered main package. helpers.mjs owns fixture sockets/timers and build/race switches. Keep test scaffolding out of production package registration.

docs.title: Focused and full commands
docs.text:
go test -count=1 ./pkg/rpc -run TestHTTPJSONPayloadShapes
go test -count=1 ./pkg/rpc -run TestCallRaw
go test -count=1 ./pkg/nodebridge
go build ./...
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
go test -race -count=1 ./...
CRPC_STANDALONE_INTEGRATION=1 CRPC_SCAFFOLD_RACE=1 go test -race -count=1 ./...

Standalone tests are opt-in, require registry/network access and an unused 4000 port, and compare the source-built CLI's actual public fallback with a deliberate local workspace. They are not proof that every newly tagged version has reached the public proxy; release testing installs that exact version separately.

From example-node run npm ci, npm run typecheck and CRPC_IPC_TEST_RACE=1 npm test. It builds TypeScript and instruments the actual Go daemon, including fault-injecting proxy tests. Ordinary root race testing does not automatically run this npm suite. Root Go ./... also excludes nested example/benchmark modules and live databases.

docs.title: Regression and cross-runtime workflow
docs.text:
Pin a baseline, reproduce over the real affected transport, add a failing test, then patch the smallest owning function. Include objects/arrays/scalars/null, malformed input, unauthorized/missing middleware, handler non-execution, typed wrappers, output errors and cleanup when relevant. Network tests need explicit shutdown/deadlines so failure does not hang a suite. Record exact commands and remaining limitations; a no-tests-matched exit0 is not regression evidence.

For shared changes, run logically equivalent Node fixtures. Use this repo's JSON fixture set and Node union/HTTP regressions rather than assuming TypeBox syntax exists here. No private review-kit parity runner is a contributor prerequisite. Do not refactor duplicated pipelines, expand stdio framing or synchronize registry mutation as a side effect of documentation. Architectural changes need explicit scope, compatibility discussion and tests across every execution site.

docs.title: Go CLI, scaffold and declaration internals
docs.text: Source: cmd/crpc-go/main.go, cmd/crpc-go/commands/init.go, cmd/crpc-go/commands/scaffold.go and cmd/crpc-go/commands/dev.go.

docs.title: Command responsibilities
docs.text:
main.go dispatches init/create:function/create:middleware/dev/build/version and holds the display version. InitProject writes the generated module, server, function/middleware examples, utilities, Makefile and .env examples. ScaffoldFunction and ScaffoldMiddleware write native registration/contracts/handlers and tests. Flags differ from Node; Go has --multipart and --desc but no --middlewares flag. Review generated imports/attachments explicitly.

Go registration depends on imports/init calls, not scanning folders on each request. The generated main imports its example functions and middleware, calls UseGlobalRegistry and starts the configured application. New packages must be imported/registered deliberately; adding files is not function discovery.

docs.title: SDK version selection is not the display version
docs.text:
scaffoldSDKVersion reads runtime/debug build information. A proper versioned module installation selects its installed module version. Missing/wrong/replaced/devel or VCS-stamped source builds select the real published older v1.0.0 fallback. Never replace that with a made-up unpublished version to make a source test appear standalone. A CLI installed from the versioned v1.0.2 module selects SDK v1.0.2. Release preparation validates this with an isolated candidate proxy; public installation must be checked again after the real tag is published.

For local SDK development, create a disposable app and explicitly use go.work to select the checkout. Its generated go.mod stays portable without parent-relative replace paths. A source-built CLI printing1.0.2 does not prove SDK v1.0.2 selection; inspect go.mod and go list -m output. See development.

docs.title: Environment and dev process
docs.text:
The generated main parses exported DOCS_ENABLED and DOCS_PATH. Omitted/blank docs boolean uses NODE_ENV!=production; trimmed case-insensitive Go boolean values are parsed, and invalid nonblank values stop startup. DOCS_PATH trims/defaults to/docs. Neither the generated program nor DevServer loads.env automatically. Dev watches Go/env files and rebuilds/restarts go run; watching an env file is not dotenv loading. Export/source trusted shell values yourself.

The generated listener still configures0.0.0.0:4000 and /rpc. PORT/HOST/RPC_PATH appear in env examples but are not consumed by that main. Do not add config semantics while fixing prose or promise a runtime setting simply because a line exists in.env. Programmatic Config remains the source of truth.

docs.title: TypeScript declaration generation
docs.text: pkg/nodebridge/ts_gen.go exports GenerateTypeScriptDeclarations, which consumes app.Functions() and returns source text. The caller writes it to a file. No crpc-go export:types command exists. The maintained example-node client imports its matching crpc.d.ts contract map; regenerate it for the actual daemon. Generated HTTP-oriented file types do not make JSON IPC transfer live files.

docs.title: Regression gates
docs.text: init_module_test.go covers portable modules/version selection; init_test.go runs actual generated server env/docs cases; init_standalone_test.go performs optional real public-SDK/workspace integration; docs_metadata_test.go checks generated metadata. Bridge ts_gen_test.go covers declaration output. Test the generated program/build/dependency selection, not only a template string. Release/version changes require the release checklist, not just a display edit.

docs.title: Go HTTP, multipart and upload ownership
docs.text: Source: pkg/rpc/engine.go, pkg/rpc/multipart.go, pkg/rpc/file.go and pkg/rpc/config.go.

docs.title: Transport and configuration
docs.text:
Config requires an explicit RpcPath and non-nil CORS configuration. Defaults include a10MiB request-body cap,20 multipart files and30s read/write/60s idle transport timeouts. Native listeners pass these settings to fasthttp; NetHTTPHandler uses a body limit wrapper/adaptor. A handler mounted in another host needs that host's own configuration too. Core config does not load environment variables.

Go HTTP JSON parses reqCtx.PostBody with encoding/json/v2. The envelope's pointer sentinel retains absent-versus-null semantics before validation. Multipart Phase1 also reads PostBody for fallback routing. Native fasthttp intake is transport- buffered, and Phase2 calls reqCtx.MultipartForm. The subsequent copy to application-owned temp files streams from file headers; this is not unbuffered end-to-end socket streaming or zero aggregate memory under concurrency.

docs.title: Routing and authorization phases
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as handleMultipartRPC
  participant P as Multipart parsers
  participant M as Middleware
  participant D as App temp directory
  participant V as Native schema / handler
  H->>H: Count headers and reject duplicates or pair errors
  alt Paired headers present
    H->>H: Validate header identifiers
  else Headerless
    H->>P: Phase1 early body routing
    P-->>H: namespace and functionName
  end
  H->>M: Resolve and execute middleware
  H->>P: Phase2 form/files
  P->>D: Create/copy app-owned temporary files
  P-->>H: Data + tracked UploadedFile values
  H->>H: Header/body consistency
  H->>V: Multipart coercion / validation / handler / output check
  H->>D: Deferred Context.Cleanup

Header counting uses VisitAll before Peek so duplicates are rejected, including case variants. Headerless Phase1 requires routing text before file parts and bounds routing fields. Phase2 still requires unambiguous body routing. Header acceleration cannot silently override conflicting body values. Middleware runs before Phase2 application writes, not before fasthttp has received the body.

Phase2 checks file count and size, normalizes text/JSON-looking values and arrays, sanitizes dangerous prototype keys, handles routing-data escape names and creates files under OS temp/crpc-uploads. Newly created directory/files request0700/0600 permissions. MIME detection inspects an initial512-byte prefix and retains declared and detected types; neither detection nor a sanitized filename sanitizes content. Config request limits and schema.File().MaxSize/AllowedMimes are separate checks.

docs.title: File lifetime and interruption
docs.text:
The parser removes already-created files if opening/sniffing/copying a later file fails. Once parsing succeeds, handleMultipartRPC immediately registers files with Context.TrackFile before subsequent consistency/schema/handler checks. Deferred Context.Cleanup removes application-owned temporary paths after request handling. Underlying fasthttp form buffering has its own lifecycle; do not count only the app temp directory when evaluating total transport resource use.

UploadedFile exposes Filename/OriginalFilename/Size/MimeType/DeclaredMimeType/ DetectedMimeType/TempPath and Bytes/Reader/SaveTo/Cleanup methods. Bytes can allocate an entire file. Reader must be closed by the caller. SaveTo creates a distinct 0600 destination atomically; it does not transfer ownership of the temporary path. Persist while handling, then pass application-owned references to background jobs.

Client disconnects/transport limits can prevent delivery of a response even when cleanup executes. Read/write timeout configuration is not a Go handler cancellation API. Tests should include failed copies, too many/oversized/empty files, duplicate routing, auth rejection, mismatch after parsing and temp cleanup, not just a successful multipart upload.

Go has fasthttp and net/http entrypoints, not seven Go framework templates. The Node adapter guide describes its different stream/Fetch boundaries. See testing for exact Go HTTP and multipart regression files.

docs.title: Native schemas, call APIs and errors
docs.text: Source: pkg/schema/rules.go, pkg/schema/validator.go, pkg/schema/jsonschema.go and the four execution sites in pkg/rpc.

docs.title: SchemaRule is native metadata plus validation rules
docs.text:
Constructors cover string, number, integer, boolean, array, object and file. Fluent methods add descriptions, requiredness, length/value/count/MIME/size rules. FromStruct uses Go types/tags to infer a contract; ToMap/ToJSONString export docs metadata. This is not a general JSON Schema evaluator or TypeBox union engine. Do not invent Nullable/Union constructors absent from the public API.

Validate recursively gathers path/message details. A nil value is rejected unless the rule is Optional; objects check known/required fields and nested rules. Optional therefore has native null behavior that is not identical to TypeBox's missing-property flag. Structs and supported JSON marshalers are normalized toward their actual JSON representation, preserving tags/omitempty/embedded-field effects. WithDefault records metadata; Validate does not automatically populate defaults.

File validation uses the native FileValidator interface for filename/size/MIME. JSON-looking multipart fields and schema-directed numeric/boolean coercion are intake behavior, not global JSON coercion. CoerceMultipartData/CoerceValue recurse through declared structures before multipart input validation. Keep ordinary JSON validation strict and compare logical cases with Node instead of copying its DSL.

docs.title: Execution-site matrix
docs.text:
Path Input + middleware Output behavior Return/error form HTTP JSON Parse v2 envelope, run middleware, native schema validation Non-nil result checked if schema present HTTP ResponseEnvelope / mapped or default200 HTTP multipart Pre-auth, parse files, consistency, coercion, input validation Non-nil result checked if schema present HTTP ResponseEnvelope and deferred file cleanup CallInMemory Native map shortcut or arbitrary JSON marshal/decode; middleware and input checks Non-nil result checked; encode into supplied target error plus output target; no HTTP status TestCaller.CallRaw Similar normalization; middleware and input checks Raw handler result currently not output-schema validated *ResponseEnvelope,error; local marshal failures can be Go errors Unix/stdio bridge Decode BridgeRequest, then CallInMemory Inherits CallInMemory; response encoding has omitempty BridgeResponse with ID/status/data/error, not HTTP envelope

This matrix is descriptive, not a request to harmonize/refactor behavior. In CallInMemory errors may contain less field detail than CallRaw/HTTP; not-found, output mismatch, nil output and ordinary error formatting can differ. CallRaw's name means an envelope result, not unchecked input or a second transport parser.

docs.title: Errors and serialization
docs.text:
pkg/rpc/errors.go defines AppError/codes/ValidationErrorDetail. HTTP dispatchError extracts structured application errors and sendErrorResponse creates the envelope. UseHttpStatusCodes chooses the explicit status mapper; otherwise handled application and parser errors return200. A library/framework framing rejection or custom route has its own status/body boundary.

HTTP engine and native schema normalization use encoding/json/v2 in this release; CallInMemory/CallRaw/bridge adapters also contain encoding/json v1 paths. They are not universally identical parsers. Test duplicate members, typed maps, nil outputs, large numbers and custom marshalers explicitly when relevant. JSON input shape preservation does not imply identical output-null/omitempty bytes across runtimes.

docs.title: Tests for a safe change
docs.text: Use schema/schema_test.go for native rules; rpc/http_json_shapes_test.go plus its checked-in testdata for HTTP omission/null/arrays/scalars; caller_test.go for CallInMemory and typed inputs; testing_test.go for CallRaw shape/validation/auth and Go error-versus-envelope conventions. Assert no handler invocation on invalid input and that middleware still runs at the expected stage. Changing typed wrappers also needs real IPC/file injection coverage. See testing.
